lots.what_it_is: 9ct yellow gold shield signet ring, worn engraved monogram, 4.6g stated, size W (gents size). No stones.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2 clearly shows a rectangular 9CT punch inside the band (read, sharp). Photo 1: shield face with a very worn engraved monogram, heavy surface scratching, and a dark line running down the right-hand shoulder that looks like a crack or open split in the metal (cropped and enlarged), plus a second short line near it. Could be an old solder seam or resize join, but it reads as a crack. The small V cuts at the shoulders are part of the design.
lots.condition: Worn and scratched; monogram rubbed; probable crack or split at one shoulder, so treat as gold value (near scrap) rather than a wearable signet.

lots.dropped_entries: Dropped Lawsons via Invaluable (page opened): it is a SOLD lot whose price is hidden ('Sold: Log in to view'), estimate $100-180, Nov 2020. Not UNSOLD as the researcher filed it, no price seen, and outside 24 months, so unusable. Dropped Chilton's Antiques $895 (curl HTTP 403, snippet only; diamond-set dealer retail, not comparable). Dropped Gumtree $499 Wallace Bishop with diamond (HTTP 403, snippet only, diamond-set, not comparable). Dropped Etsy $166.80 (HTTP 403, snippet only, weight unknown). All researcher Gowans entries were confirmed in the API with matching price, bids and date; I relabelled the 4.5-4.6g plain rings as same item and the small signets as category guide.
lots.guide_summary: All 13 surviving entries are SOLD hammers at Gowans (no unsold, no asking survives). Same-weight plain 9ct rings (4.5-4.6g) made $250-$300 hammer over the last year; the wider 4.2-5.1g group ran $150-$400. Scrap 9ct at Gowans made about $53/g in Sep 2026 (about $245 for 4.6g). Melt today: gold US$4,149.70/oz (gold-api.com, 14 Oct 2026) x AUD 1.4328 per USD (open.er-api.com) = A$191.2/g pure, 9ct A$71.7/g, so about A$330 for 4.6g. Melt is a floor reference, not a sale. All AUD, no other FX.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD (4.5-4.6g plain 9ct, last 24 months) = $250 (lot 371794, Nov 2025). 250 / 1.198 = 208.7, round down to $205 (all-in $245.59, about 74% of today's A$330 melt). If the 5.1g $150 outlier were treated as same item it would be $125, but it is a different weight. The scrap rate ($53/g x 4.6 = $245) agrees with $205 being a sensible cap given the likely crack. Flip: likely resale $260 (middle of the 4.5g Gowans hammers, or a gold buyer at about 80% of melt, $264), less 15% selling fees ($39) = $221; 221 / 2.396 = 92.2, round down to $90. Postage $0 (sell locally). Pickup Moonah, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: 9CT mark read clearly and many Gowans SOLD results opened, which would be High, but the apparent crack at the shoulder makes condition uncertain, so Medium.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the dark line on the right shoulder of lot 10 a crack or split in the band, or a solder/resize seam? Any other marks beside 9CT (maker, sponsor)? Confirm 4.6g weight.

lots.what_it_is: Scott carbon road bike (Gowans title: SCOTT ROAD BIKE - BLACK - FP242), frame shape consistent with a rim-brake Scott Addict, matte black. Shimano 11-speed mechanical groupset (4-arm Hollowtech crank and lever shape suggest 105 R7000 or similar; not read), Shimano WH-RS11 wheels ('RS11' visible on the rims, not Fulcrum as the researcher said), rim brakes and quick-release skewers.
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo. Brand from the Gowans title, not legible on the frame. Rims read 'RS11' (Shimano WH-RS11 entry wheels). Front rim-brake caliper and quick-release confirmed on enlargement. Cable-operated Shimano levers, 2x crankset, 11-speed style. Profile Design clip-on aero bars with green tape over black tape, worn and dirty bar tape, saddle bag, rear light, bottle cage. Frame size unknown, looks medium-small.
lots.condition: Used, worn bar tape, general grime; no damage visible at this size, but carbon frame condition cannot be judged from one photo.
